newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada unfazed by possible EU challenge on films.
newsitem.headline: Canada unfazed by possible EU challenge on films.

text.p: Industry Minister John Manley said on Friday he was not concerned about a European Union (EU) challenge to Canada's film distribution policy at the World Trade Organization (WTO).

The EU said this week it was considering mounting a WTO challenge of Canada's refusal to let the Dutch firm PolyGram NV -- 75 percent owned by Philips Electronics NV -- distribute foreign films in Canada.
"If they decide to put it to a (dispute) panel then we'll deal with that," Manley told reporters.
"In the meantime, the advice that I've received is that our film distribution policy is consistent with our WTO obligations and that we wouldn't have any difficulty with such a challenge."

Canada's decided last month to allow the Dutch music and entertainment group to set up a film production subsidiary in Canada but continued to refuse to allow it to distribute lucrative foreign films in Canada.
PolyGram considers the new arrangement to be an interim stage, according to the EU ambassador to Canada, John Beck.

The Europeans consider Canada's culture protection policy discriminatory because under a "grandfathering" arrangement Hollywood distributors have been allowed to continue distributing U.S. films in Canada.
"Our policy applies equally to all countries who wish to establish new distribution facilities in Canada. It's not discriminatory, which I understood was the essence of their allegations."
